doc: Proof-mutation manifest for verify-proof-mutation (the proof-side analogue of cargo-mutants). Each entry mutates the Lean source in a way whose outcome is KNOWN, and the runner (scripts/check_proof_mutations.py) asserts the rebuild matches `expect`. A green-when-it-should-be-red = a vacuity (V4 dead conjunct) or a broken claim, caught. Most entries EXECUTE a specific falsifiability claim AXIOM_STATUS.json makes in prose ('deleting X leaves theft_free proven', 'A3.4 has zero consumers', 'reachable_implies_combinedCap is load-bearing for the P1 discharge'). DELETION is done by RENAMING the declaration (single-line, materially-different by construction, robust to whitespace) so every downstream reference becomes an unknown identifier. Each mutation is applied to ONE file, fully rebuilt (lake build SphincsCVerify rebuilds the changed module + all reverse-dependencies — mathlib stays cached), then ALWAYS reverted. CLOSES V4 (dead conjunct) + the load-bearingness claims; does NOT close V7 (latent-FALSE axiom — a false axiom that still type-checks is invisible to mutation while lean/ is mathlib-free) or V11 (wrong spec). See docs/verification/fv-adversarial-review-playbook.md §A.

tiers.default: the curated 8 (load-bearing premises + non-load-bearing markers + the P1 non-vacuity guard)
tiers.full: default + the corollary bridge-axiom load-bearing checks (~13 rebuilds)

mutations.rationale: PERMANENT CANARY. Breaks theft_free's proof with an unknown identifier. If this does NOT fail the build, the mutation harness itself is broken (it cannot detect a break in the most important file) — and every other result is meaningless. Non-negotiable per the adversarial-review playbook.
A3.1 is the load-bearing verifier<->bytecode bridge. theft_free's existence conjunct rewrites the deployed verifier into the Lean model via it. Renaming it must break theft_free.
